title: Expedition 33 Weapons Tier List - Best Ranked
description: Definitive weapons tier list for Expedition 33 ranking S through B tier weapons for all characters with comparison analysis and upgrade priority guide.

sections.title: Ranking Criteria
sections.content:
This tier list evaluates every weapon in Expedition 33 based on several factors that determine real combat effectiveness across the full game.

Evaluation Factors

  • Base Power + Scaling: Raw damage output at full upgrade level
  • Passive Synergy: How well milestone passives (Level 4/10/20) synergize with the character's kit
  • Availability: When in the game you can obtain it — earlier is better for progression value
  • Build Flexibility: Does it work with multiple skill builds or lock you into one path?
  • Endgame Viability: Does it remain competitive against Endless Tower and Level 50+ bosses?

Tier Definitions

TierMeaning
S TierBest-in-slot for endgame. Defines optimal builds. Worth building entire strategies around.
A TierExcellent weapons that perform at near-optimal levels. Viable alternatives to S Tier with different playstyles.
B TierSolid weapons for progression. Good during their level range but eventually replaced by higher tiers.

Weapons below B Tier are excluded — they're usable for progression but outclassed quickly. Focus resources on A and S Tier weapons.

sections.title: S Tier Weapons
sections.content:
These are the definitive best weapons in Expedition 33. Each one enables dominant builds that trivialize late-game content when fully invested.

Cleim (Lune) — Endless Tower Reward

The strongest Lune weapon. Creates an ethereal sword dealing additional damage with every skill cast. Stacking different Stains via Elemental Trick doubles your subsequent turn's damage. Unmatched damage ceiling when played optimally.

Esquim (Lune) — Verso's Drafts Paint Cage

Converts all Stains to Dark Stains on Base Attack, then Lightning Dance and similar multi-hit skills deal 300% more damage. Slightly easier to use than Cleim with nearly comparable output. Available mid-game.

Charnon (Sciel) — Grour in Renoir's Drafts

100% Critical Chance during Twilight. Applies Foretell on crits. +20% stacking damage per turn without taking damage (up to 5 stacks). Transforms Sciel into an untouchable DPS monster for players who can parry consistently.

Medalum (Maelle) — Gestral Arena (as Maelle)

Starts every fight in Virtuose Stance. This single passive eliminates the setup turns other Maelle builds require. Available early-game and remains relevant throughout due to the massive action economy advantage.

Ballaro (Monoco) — Late-game

Level 10/20 passives provide AP to all party members on Upgraded Skills. Transforms Monoco into the party's AP engine, enabling your DPS characters to use expensive abilities every turn. Unmatched support value.

Jarum (Maelle) — Chromatic Jar, west of Gestral Village

Stacks Burn damage AND switches to Virtuose Stance on counterattack (Level 4). Combined with consistent parrying, Maelle never leaves Virtuose Stance and amplifies all Burn synergies.

sections.title: A Tier Weapons
sections.content:
Excellent weapons that define strong builds. Often the best choice until S Tier becomes available, or viable endgame alternatives with different playstyles.

Snowim (Lune) — Gargant in Frozen Hearts/Flying Manor

Restores HP at turn start, provides Stains and AP at higher levels. The ultimate survival weapon that keeps Lune alive through extended fights. Best for healer-focused Lune builds where staying alive matters more than raw damage.

Trebuchim (Lune) — Ancient Sanctuary

Generates random Stains on Free Aim shots. The most flexible mid-game option enabling Elemental Genesis combos from any starting position. Outclassed by Esquim/Cleim for pure damage but unmatched for versatility.

Tisseron (Sciel) — Sirene Story Boss

Increases Twilight damage with Sun Skills and grants an extra turn when entering Twilight. More aggressive than Charnon with less defensive utility. Best for "enter Twilight and immediately nuke" playstyles.

Lithum (Maelle) — The Reacher (Maelle Relationship 5)

Capitalizes on Marked enemies with increased damage. Switches to Virtuose on counterattack at Level 10. Requires Mark application setup but has higher theoretical damage ceiling against single targets than Jarum.

Dualiso (Gustave/Verso) — Dualliste Boss

Low base damage but effectively grants double turns. First turn builds Rank (Verso) or Overcharge (Gustave); second turn unleashes full-power attacks. Unique playstyle that rewards patient, strategic players.

Lanceram (Gustave/Verso) — Spring Meadows

Consistently high power with no special gimmicks. Available extremely early and remains competitive throughout due to solid stat scaling. The reliable choice that never disappoints.

Deminerim (Lune) — Demineur Quest, Flying Waters

Reduces Electrify AP cost to zero. Enables infinite Lightning spam for free, particularly strong in fights where Lune has other AP demands. Excellent early-to-mid game.

sections.title: B Tier Weapons
sections.content:
Solid progression weapons that serve you well during their level range. Worth upgrading partially but don't invest maximum materials — save those for S/A Tier weapons.

Gustave/Verso Swords

  • Abysseram: Good early-game from Flying Waters Bourgeon. Decent power until Lanceram surpasses at higher upgrade levels.
  • Sakaram: Ancient Sanctuary drop. Fills the gap between Lanceram and Dualiso availability.
  • Cultam: Purchased from Grandis Merchant. Serviceable mid-game option with no standout features.
  • Gaulteram: Provides elemental diversity for Verso. Useful against bosses weak to its element.

Lune Staves

  • Lighterim: First weapon available. Good for Burn builds early on but quickly outclassed by Deminerim and Trebuchim.
  • Coralim: Cold-focused weapon from Stone Wave Cliffs. Solid for Cold/Earth builds but the Cold playstyle is generally weaker than Lightning or Multi-Element.
  • Betelim: Earth weapon. Niche use for Break-focused builds but Earth skills are primarily utility, not DPS.

Maelle Rapiers

  • Brulerum: First Maelle weapon from Flying Waters. Fine for progression, immediately replaced by Medalum.
  • Sekarum: Gestral Village purchase. Adequate if you missed Medalum from the Arena.
  • Coldum: Grandis Merchant. Mid-game filler before Jarum/Lithum become available.

Sciel Weapons

  • Lusteson: From Chromatic Luster in Forgotten Battlefield. Good transition weapon before Tisseron/Charnon.
  • Ramasson: Early Sciel weapon. Gets the job done until better options appear.

sections.title: Upgrade Priority
sections.content:
Materials are limited, especially rare endgame materials. Here's the optimal order to invest your upgrade resources for maximum party effectiveness.

Priority 1: Your Primary DPS Weapon

Upgrade your main damage dealer's weapon first. This is typically:

  • Maelle: Medalum early → Jarum/Lithum when available
  • Sciel: Charnon or Tisseron once obtained
  • Lune (DPS build): Esquim or Cleim for damage-focused builds

Priority 2: Lune's Weapon (If Healer Build)

Weapon upgrades increase Lune's healing output alongside damage. A stronger weapon means better heals and more effective combat contribution even in a support role.

Priority 3: Secondary DPS

Your third party member's weapon. Usually Verso's Dualiso or whichever character fills your second DPS slot.

Priority 4: Support Weapons (Passive-Gated)

Weapons like Ballaro (Monoco) primarily matter at milestone levels (10 and 20) where passives unlock. You can leave them at Level 10 until other weapons are maxed, then push to 20 later.

Material Conservation Tips

  • Don't upgrade B Tier weapons past Level 8 — you'll replace them soon
  • Save all rare materials (Cores, Essences) for S/A Tier weapons
  • It's better to have one maxed weapon than three half-upgraded ones
  • The Endless Tower is the best endgame material farm — complete it to max remaining weapons
